t: PX4 Autopilot: What PX4 Is: The Flight Stack
title: PX4 Autopilot: What PX4 Is: The Flight Stack
description: PX4 is the software that flies the drone: it reads the IMU, barometer, GPS, and compass; fuses them into a position estimate with the EKF2 estimator; runs the position, velocity, and attitude control loops; drives the motors or servos; and executes missions — all at hundreds of hertz on a Pixhawk-class flight controller. QGroundControl is its ground station. PX4 flies everything from racing quads to survey fixed-wings to VTOLs, and its permissive BSD license is why the commercial drone industry standardizes on it.
key_facts: Runs at hundreds of Hz on Pixhawk

t: PX4 Autopilot: EKF2: Knowing Where You Are
title: PX4 Autopilot: EKF2: Knowing Where You Are
description: A drone cannot control what it cannot estimate. EKF2 (extended Kalman filter) fuses IMU, GPS, barometer, magnetometer, and optical flow into one position/velocity/attitude estimate, tracking sensor biases and rejecting outliers. When GPS degrades, the filter coasts on the IMU; when a sensor fails, innovation gates reject it. Tuning EKF2 is understanding noise: the process-noise parameters say how much you trust the model versus the sensors. Good estimates make everything downstream easy.
key_facts: Fuses IMU, GPS, baro, mag, optical flow
Per-sensor trust published with the estimate

t: PX4 Autopilot: Control Loops: Position to Motors
title: PX4 Autopilot: Control Loops: Position to Motors
description: PX4 controls in cascades: the position controller turns a waypoint into velocity setpoints, the velocity controller into attitude/thrust setpoints, the attitude controller into body rates, and the rate controller into motor commands — each loop faster than the one above it. The mixer maps control outputs to the airframe's motors. Tuning is bottom-up: rates first, then attitude, then velocity, then position. A well-tuned drone feels locked in; a badly tuned one oscillates, and oscillation near the ground is how drones die.
key_facts: Cascaded loops: position to body rates

t: PX4 Autopilot: Flight Modes: From Manual to Mission
title: PX4 Autopilot: Flight Modes: From Manual to Mission
description: PX4's modes are the pilot's vocabulary: Manual/Stabilized for direct control, Altitude and Position for assisted flight, Mission for autonomous waypoint execution, Return for automatic homecoming, Hold, Offboard (companion computer commands), and the safety modes. Mode transitions are guarded — the stack refuses Mission mode without a valid position estimate. Understanding modes is understanding what the drone is allowed to decide versus what the human decides.

t: PX4 Autopilot: Your First Flight: SITL Simulation
title: PX4 Autopilot: Your First Flight: SITL Simulation
description: Nobody's first PX4 flight is on hardware: SITL (software-in-the-loop) runs the exact flight stack on your laptop against a simulated vehicle in Gazebo, with QGroundControl connected as if it were real. You arm, take off, fly a mission, and trigger Return — learning the stack's behavior with zero crash cost. The discipline is that SITL must be boring before hardware: if the mission surprises you in sim, it will surprise you worse in the air.
key_facts: SITL runs the real stack on a laptop

t: PX4 Autopilot: Missions: Waypoints, Geofences, Rally Points
title: PX4 Autopilot: Missions: Waypoints, Geofences, Rally Points
description: PX4 missions are more than waypoint lists: survey patterns, geofences (keep-in polygons and keep-out zones), rally points for emergency landing, and mission commands (do-jump loops, camera triggers). The geofence is the safety contract — breach it and the stack executes the fenced action (Return or land). Mission planning in QGroundControl visualizes all of it. The professional habit is planning the emergency before the mission: where does it land if everything fails?

t: PX4 Autopilot: Safety: Failsafes and Return Logic
title: PX4 Autopilot: Safety: Failsafes and Return Logic
description: PX4's failsafes are the reason it is trusted: RC loss, datalink loss, GPS loss, low battery, and geofence breach each trigger configured responses — usually Return or Land, with hysteresis so a flickering link does not cause mode thrashing. The return logic computes whether battery suffices to get home and acts early, not at 5%. Failsafe tuning is safety engineering: every threshold is a bet about the vehicle's real behavior, validated in SITL first.

t: PX4 Autopilot: Defensive Uses: Survey and Monitoring
title: PX4 Autopilot: Defensive Uses: Survey and Monitoring
description: PX4's defensive applications are eyes that do not blink: perimeter survey fixed-wings flying repeatable patterns, infrastructure inspection multicopters with geofenced corridors, and search-support aircraft covering grids while the crew watches the feed. The stack's value is repeatability — the tenth flight follows the same line as the first — plus the safety architecture that lets it fly beyond line of sight where regulations permit. The human decides the mission; the stack executes it precisely.

t: PX4 Autopilot: Tuning: From Oscillations to Locked-In
title: PX4 Autopilot: Tuning: From Oscillations to Locked-In
description: PX4 tuning is a method: fly the rate loops first, use the FFT-based filter tuning to kill gyro noise, set the notch filters, then work up the cascade with step-response tests. The log analysis tools (Flight Review) show tracking error per loop — tune until the error is small and the motors are not hot. Autotune helps, but understanding what it changed is mandatory: a tune you cannot explain is a tune you cannot trust when the airframe changes.
key_facts: FFT filter tuning kills gyro noise

t: PX4 Autopilot: Companion Computers and Offboard Control
title: PX4 Autopilot: Companion Computers and Offboard Control
description: PX4 flies the vehicle; companion computers do the thinking: a Jetson-class board runs vision, avoidance, or mission logic and commands PX4 over MAVLink in Offboard mode. The interface contract is setpoints at a minimum rate — stop sending and the stack falls back to Hold. This separation is architectural wisdom: the hard-real-time flight control stays on the flight controller, and the best-effort AI stays where a crash does not crash the aircraft.

t: PX4 Autopilot: Debugging: Flight Review and Log Analysis
title: PX4 Autopilot: Debugging: Flight Review and Log Analysis
description: Every PX4 flight produces a ULog — the black box with every sensor, estimate, and actuator command at full rate. Flight Review plots it in the browser: tracking errors, vibration levels, GPS jamming indicators, power draw. The debugging ladder is vibration (mechanical), then estimator health, then loop tracking, then mission logic. Most 'software bugs' are loose propellers — the log shows it in the vibration plot before you touch a parameter.

title: PX4 Autopilot: HIL: Hardware-in-the-Loop Testing
description: HIL closes the loop with real hardware: the actual Pixhawk runs the real PX4 stack, but its sensor inputs come from the simulator and its actuator outputs go back to the sim. This tests the exact binary that will fly — including hardware quirks — against scenarios too dangerous for the field: GPS loss at altitude, motor failure, geofence breaches. HIL is the gate between SITL and first flight for any serious program.
key_facts: Fault suite green before first flight

t: PX4 Autopilot: Airframe Configuration: Mixing and Geometry
title: PX4 Autopilot: Airframe Configuration: Mixing and Geometry
description: PX4 supports hundreds of airframes because the mixer is data: geometry files map control outputs to motors and servos for quads, hexas, fixed-wings, VTOLs, and rovers. Configuring a new airframe is describing its physics — motor positions, rotation directions, control surface linkages — then verifying with motor tests and a tethered hover. The airframe file is the vehicle's identity to the stack.
key_facts: Signed vehicle record binds tune and thresholds

t: PX4 Autopilot: Real-World Pattern: Corridor Inspection
title: PX4 Autopilot: Real-World Pattern: Corridor Inspection
description: A complete pattern: a hexacopter flies a geofenced power-line corridor monthly — same waypoints, same altitude, camera triggering at stations. PX4 executes the mission; the companion computer watches the wire with a vision model; anomalies are geotagged. The crew reviews thumbnails, not hours of video. When the corridor changes, the mission is replanned in QGroundControl and re-validated in SITL before flight.

title: PX4 Autopilot: Mastery: The Flight-Stack Playbook
description: PX4 mastery is aviation discipline expressed in software: estimator fluency, cascade tuning, failsafe engineering, mission planning with the emergency first, and log-driven debugging.
